bull.t: Strong revenue growth and customer demand
bull.b: Broad-based growth across restaurant expansion, comparable sales, and traffic indicates durable customer demand rather than reliance on openings alone. Sustained visit frequency and revenue momentum can support operating leverage, brand reach, and continued reinvestment over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Scalable expansion and productive new restaurants
bull.b: The combination of rapid unit growth, strong new-restaurant productivity, and high average unit volume supports a credible expansion model. Productive openings can compound revenue and cash generation while increasing brand presence, provided execution remains consistent as the footprint scales.

bull.t: Strong liquidity and improving cash generation
bull.b: A substantial cash position, no debt outstanding in the reported quarter, and committed revolver capacity provide meaningful financial flexibility for restaurant growth. Positive free cash flow and improving operating cash generation also strengthen the company’s ability to fund expansion internally.

bear.b: The sharp decline from unusually high 2024 profitability shows that earnings margins are not yet consistently durable at peak levels. Lower current margins leave less room to absorb cost inflation or execution variability and may constrain the pace at which revenue growth converts into earnings.

bear.t: Food, labor, and delivery costs pressure margins
bear.b: Multiple operating cost categories are rising simultaneously, creating a sustained challenge for restaurant-level profitability. Food and labor inflation, fuel surcharges, and delivery-related expense pressure could limit operating leverage unless pricing, productivity initiatives, or sales growth offset the higher cost base.

bear.t: Cash conversion remains limited by reinvestment needs
bear.b: Although cash generation has improved, relatively low free-cash-flow conversion indicates that substantial capital spending and reinvestment continue to absorb earnings. Historical volatility in free cash flow makes internally funded expansion less predictable and may limit cash available for other capital priorities.
